Gowans Auctions, Moonah. Two online auctions closing Tue 6 Oct 2026

Gowans tracker

UPDATE Monday 5 Oct, 8 PM Hobart: bids on all 285 lots were refreshed, and both auctions close tomorrow (Fine Art from 6 PM, Special Antique from 7 PM). The catalogues are unchanged since the scan, and no new Gowans auction is posted yet. Bidding has moved a lot: both McWilliams panels (lots 63 and 72) are now well above their ceilings ($4,575 and $4,150 against a KEEP max of $3,670), and the sovereign set (174), silver teapot (204), gold coin (152) and Edwardian basket (188) are also past theirs. Picks that still have headroom under their ceilings: the Omega Constellation (123, no bids), Nyakul Dawson (19, $300), the two 1984 Penfolds Grange (184 and 189, no bids), the Max Angus (78) and Carington Smith (83) watercolours, and the Pro Hart etchings (17 and 51, no bids). Every one of the 285 lots in both Gowans auctions was scanned with every photo viewed. The 120 strongest candidates got a market pass that keeps sold prices, unsold results and asking prices separate, and an Opus check of each. The best-supported picks are the two small McWilliams panels (lots 63 and 72, both at $1,525 against recent sales of $4,400 to $9,000 for small McWilliams panels), the Max Angus and Carington Smith watercolours (66, 78, 83), two 1984 Penfolds Grange (184, 189), the Omega Constellation (123), the Unknown Warrior sovereign set (174) and the Nyakul Dawson painting (19). Several silver and gold lots need a hallmark, weight or fill check at the preview before you rely on them. Maximum bids come only from sold prices in the last 24 months, and where the comp is only close to the item, the card says so. Bids move fast near the close, so check them before you act.

Run details

Mode
Lot pages and photos fetched directly with curl from gowans.bidsonline.com.au. Read-only: no bids, logins, watches or forms.
Buyer's premium
19.8% (GST inclusive) as shown on every lot page. Gowans' support page still says 17.6%, so the two disagree. This page uses 19.8%, so all-in = hammer x 1.198. Ask Gowans on (03) 6278 1600 to confirm before you bid.
Collection
Pickup from 37 Main Road, Moonah. Inbound freight assumed $0 (local). No estimates are shown on this site.
Closing
Lots close in order, 30 seconds apart. Bids in the last 60 seconds reset the lot to 2 minutes.

Blocked or login sources

Resume point
Workflow run wf_0292987d-6ed (script work/wf_gowans.js in the repo). Batch files are in scans/ (g1_ and g2_), one per batch.

Assumptions
  • Both catalogues were scanned from their own index: 89 lots in the Fine Art Auction and 196 in the Special Antique Auction. All 285 were scanned with every photo viewed and none was unscanned.
  • Buyer's premium is 19.8% on every lot page but Gowans' support page says 17.6%. This page uses 19.8% (all-in = hammer x 1.198). Confirm with Gowans before you bid.
  • Gowans shows no estimates, so scoring was blind to price by design. The current bid was not used to judge value.
  • 120 candidates with a blind score of 3 or more got a market pass. The other 88 candidates and the 77 lots the scan skipped are listed in the table of every lot with a one-line photo finding and reason, but have no comps research.
  • Many sold prices come from Invaluable results data. Invaluable does not say whether these include buyer's premium, and each card notes this where it matters.
  • Where no identical item has sold, a maximum bid may rest on one close sale or on a weight-adjusted price (for example the silver teapot, lot 204). The card for each lot says which, and the confidence level reflects it.
  • Pickup only from 37 Main Road, Moonah. Inbound freight is assumed to be $0 because you are local.
  • Sources closed to this session (eBay, Wine-Searcher, Australian Whisky Auctions) were not used. Foreign currency comps are converted at the rate stated on each card.

Working and confidence

Why Medium: The inscription and art centre number are clearly read in the photos and the pages were opened. But only one recent SOLD result is truly close, and it is larger. No certificate is visible, and Invaluable does not say whether its prices include premium.

Dropped entries: Nothing dropped. Every Invaluable figure matches the artist-page JSON I parsed (17+ records), and the Newstead page shows AUD 2,800 as claimed. One correction: 'Walu' (Theodore Bruce) is 129 x 138 cm unstretched according to its lot page, so it is larger than the lot, not of unknown size. The researcher's Mossgreen AUD 22,705 record was snippet-only and is not included.

Working: Keep: the lowest close SOLD within 24 months is Walu at AUD 1,150 (13 Apr 2026). 1,150 / 1.198 = 959.9, rounded down to 955. Flip: likely resale AUD 1,150 through a mainland or Hobart auction, less 20% vendor costs (commission, photography, insurance, assumed) = 920, with outbound freight AUD 0 if consigned locally. 920 / 2.396 = 384.0, rounded down to 380. Caution: the lot is smaller than Walu, a same-size 2003 work passed in at AUD 2,000 last month, and no art centre certificate is visible, so 955 is not a cheap bid.

Ask Gowans: Does the painting come with an Irrunytju Arts certificate or any provenance paperwork? Please confirm the size (81.5 x 119.8 cm) and whether there are any losses, cracking or stains on the front or edges.

Working and confidence

Why Medium: Signature and verso artist label read in the photos. There is one close SOLD comp (page opened) plus several same-artist category sales. Premium treatment is unknown, and the verso retail price is well below auction results.

Dropped entries: Researcher supplied no entries (WebSearch budget exhausted), so nothing to drop. Excluded: two Heritage Antiques (USA) 2024 prints by a different Michael McWilliams (Civil War print artist), large linen works and painted furniture (not comparable).

Working: Only SOLD entries within 24 months that are close (same artist, medium and similar size) count. In the Looking Glass, AUD 4,400 (June 2025), is the only one that qualifies. keep = 4,400 / 1.198 = 3,672.8, rounded down to 3,670. Flip: likely resale about 4,400 at Colville or Gibson's, less about 20% vendor commission and fees = 3,520, less about $30 local delivery = 3,490. 3,490 / 2.396 = 1,456.6, rounded down to 1,455. The Gowans bid is already $1,525 (2 bids, seen 30/09/2026), above the flip maximum, so treat this as a keep only. Caution: this rests on one close comp, and premium inclusion is unknown. The artist's own 2012 retail label says $1,000, and small panels sold for $1,400 to $2,300 in 2024, so a bid near the keep maximum is at the top of the evidence.

Ask Gowans: Can you confirm the panel size and the extent of the chips on the top border edge? Is there any provenance beyond the verso entry form (the exhibition it was entered in, or a purchase receipt)?

Bishop & Miller moved from UNSOLD to SOLD (closed, reserve met, bid GBP 130).

Working: Keep: lowest surviving SOLD within 24 months = Denhams A$208.2 / 1.198 = A$173.8, round down to $170 hammer (A$204 all-in). The 2021 sale is left out for age. Flip: likely resale A$208 (Denhams) less 15% selling commission (A$31) and A$15 outbound postage = A$162 / 2.396 = A$67.6, round down to $65. Pickup Moonah, inbound $0.
